Messages.Body:
>>>>> "SEM" == Stephen E Mynhier <smy...@hubcap.clemson.edu> writes:

SEM> Well, section 8 of the rules states that:
SEM> You lose one blood from your blood pool during your untap phase for
SEM> each of your contested cards. Alternately, you can decide to discard
SEM> your contested cards (and all blood counters those cards may have on
SEM> them, to the bank).

How is this not clear? If you have a contested card, you have a choice:
1) Pay one pool
2) Yield the card

This happens during your untap phase, and if you are the last person with
a contested card it becomes your at the beginning of your next turn (not
immediately).

Messages.Body:
cfbe...@eos.ncsu.edu (Chad Franklin Bennett) writes:

>Hey everybody, I have a question I need a little help with.
>I had a vampire that was about to be sent to topor through
>agrivated damage, and I offered to use a press at this time
>to continue combat. Would this be allowed?
>
I fail to see what this has to do with Malk. Dementia timing, but:

No.
A vampire being sent to torpor ends the combat (unless, of course, you
play a card that states otherwise, like undead persistence).

>cfbe...@eos.ncsu.edu

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
During untap, you choose whether to pay to keep a contested card, or
yield it. This is the only time when you can choose to yield it. I believe
the corrected rules are clearer on this, but don't seem to have them
with me.

Malkavian Dementia wears off at the beginning of your untap phase.
